hints.title: Bipartite Extremes
hints.text: To maximize squared distances between consecutive elements, successive choices should oscillate between the largest and smallest remaining values.

hints.title: Two-Pointer Interleaving
hints.text: Sort the heights and use opposite pointers to interleave the largest and smallest available heights.

hints.title: Initial Jump from Ground
hints.text: Remember to start the jump trajectory at height zero before transitioning to the first selected pillar.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def maximumCalories(self, heights: list[int]) -> int:
        # Start at 0, jump between pillars. Calories burnt = (h_next - h_curr)^2
        # Maximize sum of squared differences by alternating extremes
        h = sorted(heights)
        n = len(h)
        seq = [0]
        l, r = 0, n - 1
        turn = True
        while l <= r:
            if turn:
                seq.append(h[r])
                r -= 1
            else:
                seq.append(h[l])
                l += 1
            turn = not turn
        total = 0
        for i in range(len(seq) - 1):
            diff = seq[i + 1] - seq[i]
            total += diff * diff
        return total
```

complexity.notes: Sorting followed by linear two-pointer extreme interleaving.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating all N! jump permutations is computationally impossible.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(N) memory to store interleaved jump order.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognize that alternating opposite extremes maximizes quadratic distances.
